stem.en: A hollow in a raw potato cup filled with sugar gathers water. The same set-up with a boiled potato does not. Why?

text.en: Boiling removes all the sugar from the potato.

feedback.en: The sugar here is added to the hollow, after boiling.

text.en: A boiled potato already holds too much water to take in any more.

feedback.en: The water would be moving into the hollow, not into the potato.

text.en: Sugar does not dissolve in a boiled potato cup.

feedback.en: Sugar still dissolves. The change is in the potato cells.

text.en: Boiling kills the cells, so membranes stop working.

feedback.en: Yes. Osmosis needs a working selectively permeable membrane.

explanation.en: Water reaches the hollow by osmosis through living potato cells. In a boiled potato the cells are dead and the membranes no longer work, so osmosis does not take place.

hints.en: What must water pass through to reach the hollow?
